- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.33) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days — especially after sharp spikes or reversals.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects downward, failing to recognize sustained momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overestimates correction after strong moves, underestimates continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model is overly optimistic in early days (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising — adjust downward by 1–2% for early horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out — underestimates volatility and overestimates stability.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment shifts sharply — model reacts too slowly to sentiment reversal.
